items.title: Selected ingoing RN extension and time orientation
items.design_state: Authored conditional draft; exact direct suppliers and unresolved interfaces are recorded in batch-22.dependency-inputs.json.
items.statement:
Let $M,q_e,q_m\in\mathbb R$ be length parameters. Set
$Q^2:=q_e^2+q_m^2$ and
$$f(r):=1-\frac{2M}{r}+\frac{Q^2}{r^2}.$$
The selected ingoing RN manifold is
$$\mathcal M_{\mathrm{in}}:=\mathbb R_v\times(0,\infty)_r\times S^2,$$
where $v,r$ have units of metres, $S^2$ has unit round metric $\gamma$ and
outward area form $\omega$, and the signature is $(-,+,+,+)$. Orient the
product by $dv\wedge dr\wedge\omega$. Define
$$g_{\mathrm{in}}=-f(r)\,dv^2+2\,dv\,dr+r^2\gamma,\qquad \mathcal F_{\mathrm{in}}=-\frac{q_e}{r^2}\,dv\wedge dr+q_m\omega.$$
These are smooth on every $r>0$, including every positive root of $f$; the
domain excludes $r=0$. This is an extension of the static RN metric and field,
not a maximal extension or a specification of a source at the excluded
centre.

For the time orientation, define the global smooth fields
$$\ell:=-\partial_r,\qquad n:=\partial_v+\frac{f(r)}2\partial_r,\qquad N:=\ell+n=\partial_v+\left(\frac{f(r)}2-1\right)\partial_r.$$
The chosen future timelike field is $N$; the future cone is the component of
the timelike cone containing it. The well-definedness proof shows that $N$ is
timelike and that $\ell,n$ are future null. On $f\ne0$, the substitution
$v=t+r_*(r)$ with $r_*'=1/f$ identifies the metric and two-form with the
static dyonic RN formulas of [[def-emg-xs-rn-data]]. This coordinate
identification does not assert agreement of time orientations on the
interior static components: on $f>0$ the selected orientation agrees with
$\partial_t$, while on $f<0$ it is the opposite of the separate choice
$\partial_r$ made by that static definition.

items.title: Dyonic RN gauges and global exactness obstruction
items.design_state: Authored conditional draft; exact direct suppliers and unresolved interfaces are recorded in batch-22.dependency-inputs.json.
items.statement:
Let $J\subset(0,\infty)$ be nonempty and open, and suppose
$f(r)=1-2M/r+(q_e^2+q_m^2)/r^2\ne0$ on $J$. On the static dyonic RN
product $\mathbb R_t\times J\times S^2$, orient by $dt\wedge dr\wedge\omega$
and use the field $\mathcal F=-q_e r^{-2}dt\wedge dr+q_m\omega$. For every
sphere $S_r$,
$$\int_{S_r}\mathcal F=4\pi q_m,\qquad \int_{S_r}\star_g\mathcal F=4\pi q_e.$$
On the north and south patches it has smooth potentials
$$\mathcal A_N=-\frac{q_e}{r}dt+q_m(1-\cos\theta)d\phi,\qquad \mathcal A_S=-\frac{q_e}{r}dt-q_m(1+\cos\theta)d\phi,$$
with $d\mathcal A_N=d\mathcal A_S=\mathcal F$ and
$\mathcal A_S-\mathcal A_N=-2q_m d\phi$ on the overlap. A global smooth
real one-form potential on this sphere-containing product exists exactly
when $q_m=0$. No circle-bundle normalization or charge quantization is
imposed.

items.title: RN roots, Killing horizons and surface gravity
items.design_state: Authored conditional draft; exact direct suppliers and unresolved interfaces are recorded in batch-22.dependency-inputs.json.
items.statement:
Let $M>0$, $Q^2=q_e^2+q_m^2>0$, and use
$f(r)=1-2M/r+Q^2/r^2$ on the selected ingoing RN model. If $M^2\ge Q^2$,
the positive roots
$$r_\pm=M\pm\sqrt{M^2-Q^2}$$
are null constant-$r$ hypersurfaces. For the Killing field $\xi=\partial_v$
normalized by the displayed coordinate for which
$g(\xi,\xi)\to-1$ as $r\to\infty$, each is a Killing horizon in the
planned local sense of
[[def-emg-causal-solution-and-horizon-vocabulary]], with signed surface
gravity
$$\kappa_\pm=\frac{f'(r_\pm)}2 =\frac{r_\pm-r_\mp}{2r_\pm^2}.$$
At extremality $M^2=Q^2$, the coincident root is $r_H=M$ and
$\kappa_H=0$. If $M^2<Q^2$, $f$ has no positive root and no constant-$r$
null hypersurface of this form. These are local properties of the selected
metric; they do not classify event horizons in a maximal spacetime.

items.title: Regular RN crossings and local bifurcation extension
items.design_state: Authored conditional draft; exact direct suppliers and unresolved interfaces are recorded in batch-22.dependency-inputs.json.
items.statement:
Let $M>0$, $Q^2=q_e^2+q_m^2>0$, and $M^2\ge Q^2$ in the selected ingoing
RN model [[def-emg-xs-ingoing-rn]]. Every positive root $r_H$ of $f$ is a
regular crossing: the metric is nondegenerate and the two-form is smooth
there. If $M^2>Q^2$, set
$$r_+=M+\sqrt{M^2-Q^2},\qquad \kappa:=\frac12 f'(r_+)>0.$$
For every auxiliary length $\ell_*>0$, there is a smooth local extension
chart on $(-\varepsilon,\varepsilon)^2\times S^2$ with dimensionless
coordinates $U,V$ and
$$UV=-K(r),\qquad K(r):=\frac{r-r_+}{\ell_*}e^{2\kappa h(r)},\qquad K'(r_+)=\ell_*^{-1},$$
where $h$ is smooth. The metric and two-form have smooth coefficients on
the whole chart, including both null axes. The sphere $U=V=0$ is a regular
bifurcation sphere: the extended Killing field $\partial_v$ vanishes there.
On the dense set $UV\ne0$, the source-free RN equations of the current
[[thm-emg-xs-rn-verification]] draft apply; their residual tensors therefore
vanish on the axes as well, conditionally on that exact draft interface and
its proof status. At extremality $M^2=Q^2$, the ingoing chart remains regular
at $r_H=M$, but the simple-root construction is not asserted because
$\kappa=0$.

references.title: Sean M. Carroll, Lecture Notes on General Relativity, arXiv:gr-qc/9712019
references.locator: Chapter 7, equations (7.110)-(7.113), printed pp. 201-203 (PDF pp. 207-209): RN roots and extremal regime; the local Kruskal construction is proved here.

items.title: Regular ingoing KN metric, field and sphere axes
items.design_state: Authored conditional draft; exact direct suppliers and unresolved interfaces are recorded in batch-22.dependency-inputs.json.
items.statement:
Let $M,a,q\in\mathbb R$ have units of metres. Set
$$\Sigma=r^2+a^2\cos^2\theta,\quad \Delta=r^2-2Mr+a^2+q^2,\quad R=r^2+a^2,$$
and let $S^2=\{(X,Y,Z)\in\mathbb R^3:X^2+Y^2+Z^2=1\}$ have unit round
metric $\gamma$ and outward area form $\omega$. Define the global one-form
$\beta:=X\,dY-Y\,dX$ and the product
$$\mathcal M_{\mathrm{in}}:=\mathbb R_v\times(0,\infty)_r\times S^2,$$
oriented by $dv\wedge dr\wedge\omega$. On this product define
$$\begin{aligned}g_{\mathrm{in}}={}&-\left(1-\frac{2Mr-q^2}{\Sigma}\right)dv^2+2\,dv\,dr-2a\,dr\,\beta-2a\frac{2Mr-q^2}{\Sigma}dv\odot\beta+\Sigma\gamma+a^2\left(1+\frac{2Mr-q^2}{\Sigma}\right)\beta^2,\\\mathcal A_{\mathrm{in}}={}&-\frac{qr}{\Sigma}(dv-a\beta),\qquad \mathcal F_{\mathrm{in}}:=d\mathcal A_{\mathrm{in}},\end{aligned}$$
where $u\odot w=(u\otimes w+w\otimes u)/2$. The time-orientation field
is $$f_0:=1-\frac{2Mr-q^2}{\Sigma},\qquad N:=\partial_v-\frac{1+f_0^2}{2}\partial_r.$$
These formulas define smooth Lorentzian metric and field data on the whole
sphere for every $r>0$, including each positive root of $\Delta$; no
maximal extension, $r=0$ locus, or global uniqueness is asserted. On the
dense pole-free set where $\Delta\ne0$, they are related to the
Boyer-Lindquist data by the advanced coordinate change proved below.

The source-free geometric electrovac equations extend across $\Delta=0$
conditionally on the exact current interface of
[[thm-emg-xs-kn-verification]]: its geometric pole-free equations are used
on the dense complement of the roots and axes, and smoothness then extends
their residuals. That supplier is a current draft theorem and is not claimed
as independently accepted here.

references.locator: Sections 2.1-2.2 and 3.3, equations (2.21), (3.18)-(3.21): charged rotating coefficients and advanced coordinates regular at roots. Their signature and units are not imported.

items.title: KN Killing generators, surface gravity, area and potential
items.design_state: Authored conditional draft; exact direct suppliers and unresolved interfaces are recorded in batch-22.dependency-inputs.json.
items.statement:
Let $M>0$ and $M^2\ge a^2+q^2>0$ in the selected ingoing KN model.
For either $r_H=r_\pm=M\pm\sqrt{M^2-a^2-q^2}$ set
$R_H=r_H^2+a^2$, $\Sigma_H=r_H^2+a^2\cos^2\theta$, and
$$\chi_H=\partial_v+\Omega_H\Psi,\qquad \Omega_H=\frac{a}{R_H},$$
where $\Psi=X\partial_Y-Y\partial_X$ is the smooth rotation field on
$S^2$. The surface $r=r_H$ is a null hypersurface and $\chi_H$ is its
future null normal and Killing generator. Under the planned normalization
$d(g(\chi_H,\chi_H))=-2\kappa_H\chi_H^\flat$ in
[[def-emg-causal-solution-and-horizon-vocabulary]],
$$\kappa_H=\frac{\Delta'(r_H)}{2R_H} =\frac{r_H-r_{\mathrm{other}}}{2R_H},\qquad \operatorname{Area}(S_H)=4\pi R_H,\qquad -\mathcal A_{\mathrm{in}}(\chi_H)=\frac{q r_H}{R_H}.$$
At the double root $\kappa_H=0$. These are local geometric calculations on
the specified model; they assert no maximality or uniqueness.

items.title: Specified time Killing ergosurfaces and geodesic constants
items.design_state: Authored conditional draft; exact direct suppliers and unresolved interfaces are recorded in batch-22.dependency-inputs.json.
items.statement:
Let $M>0$ and $M^2\ge a^2+q^2>0$ in the selected ingoing KN model.
For the specified stationary field $T=\partial_v$,
$$g(T,T)=-\frac{r^2-2Mr+q^2+a^2\cos^2\theta}{\Sigma},\qquad \Sigma=r^2+a^2\cos^2\theta.$$
Define its ergoregion by $g(T,T)>0$ and its stationary-limit set by
$g(T,T)=0$, using the planned terminology in
[[def-emg-causal-solution-and-horizon-vocabulary]]. At each angle where
the discriminant is nonnegative, the stationary-limit radii are
$$r_{E\pm}(\theta)=M\pm\sqrt{M^2-q^2-a^2\cos^2\theta}.$$
If $a\ne0$, then $g(T,T)=a^2\sin^2\theta/\Sigma_H>0$ at every nonpolar
point of the outer horizon $r_+=M+\sqrt{M^2-a^2-q^2}$, and
$r_{E+}(\theta)>r_+$. The outer stationary-limit set meets the outer
horizon on the rotation axis. For each affinely parameterized geodesic,
$g(T,\dot\gamma)$ and $g(\Psi,\dot\gamma)$ are constant, where
$\Psi=X\partial_Y-Y\partial_X$ generates rotations. These statements
refer to the specified fields and model.

references.title: Sean M. Carroll, Lecture Notes on General Relativity, arXiv:gr-qc/9712019
references.locator: Chapter 7, equations (7.124)-(7.128): rotating horizon and stationary-limit surfaces; the selected-model claims are derived here.

items.title: Charged KN ring regularity obstruction
items.design_state: Authored conditional draft; exact direct suppliers and unresolved interfaces are recorded in batch-22.dependency-inputs.json.
items.statement:
For the electric KN datum with real $M,a,q$ and $q\ne0$, let
$\mathcal U$ be its Boyer-Lindquist domain $\Sigma>0$, $\Delta\ne0$,
$0<\theta<\pi$. Suppose a sequence $x_n\in\mathcal U$ and a proposed
$C^2$ Lorentzian extension $(\widetilde M,\widetilde g)$ are given, with a
smooth isometric embedding $j:\mathcal U\to\widetilde M$ onto an open
subset, $j(x_n)\to p\in\widetilde M$, and $\Sigma(x_n)\to0$.
Then no such extension exists. When $a\ne0$, the limiting coordinate locus
$r=0$, $\theta=\pi/2$ maps under
$$X=\sqrt{r^2+a^2}\sin\theta\cos\phi,\quad Y=\sqrt{r^2+a^2}\sin\theta\sin\phi,\quad Z=r\cos\theta$$
to $X^2+Y^2=a^2$, $Z=0$. When $q=0$, this charged Ricci-invariant
argument yields no obstruction and makes no vacuum Kerr claim.

items.title: Smooth causal-cone collar barrier with screen directions
items.design_state: Authored conditional draft; exact direct suppliers and unresolved interfaces are recorded in batch-22.dependency-inputs.json.
items.statement:
Consider either (i) the selected ingoing RN model with $M>0$, $Q^2>0$,
$M^2\ge Q^2$, and
$r_H=M+\sqrt{M^2-Q^2}$, or (ii) the selected ingoing KN model with $M>0$,
$M^2\ge a^2+q^2>0$, and
$r_H=M+\sqrt{M^2-a^2-q^2}$. In each case $r_H>0$. There is
$\delta>0$ and a collar
$$\mathcal C=\mathbb R_v\times(r_H-\delta,r_H+\delta)\times S^2$$
on which $\tau:=v-r$ is a smooth temporal function in the sense of
[[def-gr-causal-conditions-and-global-hyperbolicity]]: its gradient is past
timelike and $d\tau(Z)>0$ for every nonzero future causal vector $Z$. There
is a finite $C\ge0$ such that
$$dr(Z)\le C|r-r_H|\,d\tau(Z)$$
for every future causal $Z$ over the collar. On $r=r_H$ one also has
$dr(Z)\le0$. This is a local cone estimate on the two specified metrics; it
is not an event-horizon theorem.

references.title: Sean M. Carroll, Lecture Notes on General Relativity, arXiv:gr-qc/9712019
references.locator: Chapter 7, RN ingoing-coordinate discussion and null character of constant-radius roots; the local cone estimate is derived here.

references.locator: Section 3.3, equations (3.18)-(3.21): advanced coordinates and null directions near the KN horizon; the full cone bound is proved here.

items.title: Outer RN escape boundary in selected model
items.design_state: Authored conditional draft; exact direct suppliers and unresolved interfaces are recorded in batch-22.dependency-inputs.json.
items.statement:
Let $M>0$, $Q^2=q_e^2+q_m^2>0$, and $M^2\ge Q^2$. In the selected
ingoing RN model put $r_H=M+\sqrt{M^2-Q^2}$. Let $\mathcal E$ be the set
of points from which a future piecewise-$C^1$ causal path in this model
reaches arbitrarily large $r$, using the planned definition
[[def-emg-causal-solution-and-horizon-vocabulary]]. Then
$$\mathcal E=\{(v,r,\omega):r>r_H\},\qquad \partial_{\mathcal M_{\mathrm{in}}}\mathcal E=\{r=r_H\}.$$
This is the boundary of the stated escape observable on the selected
manifold. It makes no claim about conformal infinity, a maximal RN extension,
collapse, or cosmic censorship.

items.title: Outer KN escape boundary on the selected ingoing model
items.design_state: Authored conditional draft; exact direct suppliers and unresolved interfaces are recorded in batch-22.dependency-inputs.json.
items.statement:
Let $M>0$ and $M^2\ge a^2+q^2>0$ in the selected ingoing KN model. Put
$r_+=M+\sqrt{M^2-a^2-q^2}$. Let $\mathcal E$ be the set of points from
which a future piecewise-$C^1$ causal path reaches arbitrarily large $r$,
using the planned definition
[[def-emg-causal-solution-and-horizon-vocabulary]]. Then
$$\mathcal E=\{p:r(p)>r_+\},\qquad \partial_{\mathcal M_{\mathrm{in}}}\mathcal E=\{p:r(p)=r_+\}.$$
This result concerns the explicit escape observable on the selected ingoing
manifold, including the extremal case. It does not classify all maximal KN
extensions, the inner Cauchy horizon, collapse, or cosmic censorship.

items.title: Superextremal RN absence of radial horizon
items.design_state: Authored conditional draft; exact direct suppliers and unresolved interfaces are recorded in batch-22.dependency-inputs.json.
items.statement:
Let $M>0$ and $Q^2=q_e^2+q_m^2>M^2$. In the selected ingoing RN model,
$f(r)>0$ for every $r>0$, so no constant-$r$ null hypersurface arises from
a radial root. Every point has a future radial null path reaching arbitrarily
large $r$, and the escape set is the whole manifold with empty relative
boundary. The escape terminology uses the absent planned interface
[[def-emg-causal-solution-and-horizon-vocabulary]]. This is not a collapse
solution or a cosmic-censorship counterexample.

items.title: Extremal RN smooth horizon with zero kappa
items.design_state: Authored conditional draft; exact direct suppliers and unresolved interfaces are recorded in batch-22.dependency-inputs.json.
items.statement:
Let $M>0$ and $q_e,q_m\in\mathbb R$ satisfy $q_e^2+q_m^2=M^2$. Then
the selected ingoing RN model has $f(r)=(1-M/r)^2$, a double positive root
$r_H=M$, and surface gravity $\kappa_H=0$. Its ingoing metric remains
nondegenerate at $r=M$. The simple-root bifurcation chart constructed in
[[thm-emg-xs-rn-crossing]] requires $\kappa>0$ and does not apply here. No
separate extremal bifurcation chart or physical realization is asserted.

items.title: Nonbounding sphere carries source-free charge flux
items.design_state: Authored conditional draft; exact direct suppliers and unresolved interfaces are recorded in batch-22.dependency-inputs.json.
items.statement:
On a sphere-containing dyonic RN domain with $q_m\ne0$, the global closed
field has nonzero flux through each sphere $S_r$. Each such sphere is a
nonbounding finite smooth singular cycle in the field domain; local
north/south potentials exist but no global real one-form potential does.
On a finite full-sphere KN exterior annulus, the same conclusion holds
conditionally for a constant dual rotation with $q\sin\beta\ne0$, under
the exact current batch-21 draft interface. Neither statement gives a
magnetic source, charge quantization, or an empirical observation.
